project.name: motif
project.description: AI-powered platform where founders validate startup ideas and connect with VCs through an admin-curated pipeline. Vite + React + TypeScript SPA backed by Supabase and a Spring Boot AI backend.

nodes.name: IdeaAnalyserPage.tsx
nodes.summary: Main founder-facing idea analysis page: accepts a title/description (or PDF upload parsed with pdfjs), warms the backend, starts and polls async AI analysis jobs, renders sanitised scores/market/competitor results, and saves to idea_analyses or shares to community_ideas.
nodes.languageNotes: Very large single React component (~2k lines) with job-resume logic via refs and sessionStorage; a strong candidate for decomposition into sub-components and hooks.

nodes.name: PitchCreatorPage.tsx
nodes.summary: Pitch deck creator page that collects idea details, runs a backend pitch-generation job with polling/resume, persists pitches to Supabase, logs activity, and exports the deck to PDF with jsPDF.

nodes.name: ProfilePage.tsx

nodes.name: safeFetch.ts
nodes.summary: Safe wrappers around Supabase list, count and existence queries that convert expected RLS permission denials and missing-table errors into empty/zero/false fallbacks instead of throwing.

nodes.name: safeFetchCount

nodes.name: safeFetchExists
nodes.summary: Runs an existence query and returns false on RLS or missing-table errors.

tour.title: App Boot Sequence
tour.description: Everything starts in index.html, which provides the #root element and loads src/main.tsx as an ES module. main.tsx mounts the React app inside GoogleOAuthProvider and BrowserRouter and pulls in the global Tailwind CSS. Keep the README open next to it: it describes Motif's three roles (founder, VC, admin) and the admin-curated pipeline that links them, which is the story the rest of this tour follows.
tour.languageLesson: Vite treats index.html as the real entry point. The <script type="module" src="/src/main.tsx"> tag is what tells Vite where your TypeScript module graph begins, so there is no separate webpack-style entry config.

tour.title: Routing by Role
tour.description: App.tsx is the hub of the frontend: it declares every route (public, founder, VC and admin trees), handles dark mode and logout, and pre-warms the backend on load. Each protected tree is wrapped in ProtectedRoute, which requires a signed-in user with a loaded profile and an allowed role, while RoleRedirect sends a user to their own dashboard after login. Both read from types/roles.ts, the single source of truth for the UserRole enum, super_admin bypass and each role's default landing route.
tour.languageLesson: React Router guards are plain components: ProtectedRoute either renders its children (or an <Outlet/>) or returns <Navigate to=...>. Because routing is just JSX, access control lives in the component tree rather than in a separate config file.

tour.title: Sign-In and UserContext
tour.description: AuthPage handles sign-up and sign-in through Supabase Auth (email/password and LinkedIn OIDC), with a remember-me option. supabase.ts creates the single shared Supabase client and uses that remember-me choice to store the session in localStorage or sessionStorage. UserContext listens for auth state changes, loads the matching row from the profiles table and exposes role flags (isFounder, isVC, isAdmin). Those flags are what ProtectedRoute and RoleRedirect from Step 2 use to decide where a user can go.
tour.languageLesson: React Context with a custom hook avoids passing the user through every component as props. Any component can read the current auth state, and when onAuthStateChange fires, every consumer re-renders together.

tour.title: Founder Submits an Idea
tour.description: IdeaAnalyserPage is the main founder screen. A founder types a title and description, or uploads a PDF that pdfjs parses in the browser. The page starts an AI analysis job, polls it until it finishes, shows the sanitised scores and market and competitor results, and saves them to the idea_analyses table or shares them to the community feed. SavedAnalysisPage reopens a stored analysis later in read-only mode, so you can see how a saved row is shown again.

tour.title: AI Analysis Pipeline
tour.description: This step follows what happens behind the Analyse button from Step 4. aiAnalysis.ts starts and polls async analysis jobs on the separate Spring Boot backend through api-client.ts, which attaches the Supabase JWT from Step 3, sets timeouts with AbortController and retries failures caused by cold starts. The backend runs on Render's free tier and goes to sleep when idle, so serverWarmup.ts pings /api/ping as soon as the app loads and exposes waitUntilWarm so the analyser can wait for the server before it starts a job. analysisValidator.ts then checks the raw LLM output: it clamps scores, adds disclaimers to suspicious numbers and converts older result formats into a SafeAnalysisResult.
tour.languageLesson: Async job polling (start a job, get an id, poll its status until it is done) avoids HTTP timeouts on slow LLM calls. In TypeScript, an AbortController passed as fetch's signal gives each request a hard deadline, and clearTimeout in a finally block keeps the timer from leaking.

tour.title: From Idea to Startup
tour.description: Once an idea is analysed, the founder can submit it for review. SubmitStartupPage collects the pitch details (industry, stage, funding ask) and calls startupService.createStartup. The startup is stored in the same idea_analyses table with a status field, which drives the whole pipeline. ideasService lists a founder's ideas without duplicates and moves them into review, and StartupDetailPage shows a founder their startup along with its intro requests and connected VCs.

tour.title: Admin Approves Startups
tour.description: Admins work inside AdminLayout, a separate portal shell with its own navigation and error boundary. On AdminStartups they filter submissions by status and approve or reject them after a ConfirmDialog, and the founder is notified of the decision. AdminIntroRequests is the second checkpoint: an admin must approve any VC-founder introduction before it goes ahead. roleVerification.ts runs a fast admin check before these database writes, so the UI guards from Step 2 are not the only protection.

tour.title: VC Browsing and Intros
tour.description: VCs get their own shell, VCLayout. VCStartups lists only the idea_analyses rows that an admin approved in Step 7. On VCStartupDetail a VC can request an introduction, and introRequestService records it and checks the VC's role. The request then goes back to the admin queue in AdminIntroRequests, so the admin team sits between every founder and VC.

tour.title: Supabase Data Services
tour.description: Every step so far has used the shared Supabase client from Step 3, which is the most depended-on file in the graph. notificationService links the roles together: it sends the 'startup submitted', 'approved' and 'intro requested' notifications and keeps the NotificationBell up to date through realtime subscriptions. safeFetch wraps list, count and existence queries so that expected row-level-security denials return empty results instead of crashing a dashboard. REALTIME_SETUP.md explains the publication setup that realtime updates depend on.
tour.languageLesson: A Supabase realtime subscription (supabase.channel(...).on('postgres_changes', ...).subscribe()) returns a channel that must be removed in the useEffect cleanup. If it is not, every re-mount adds another listener and notifications start arriving more than once.

tour.title: Database Schema and RLS
tour.description: The idea_analyses table stores ideas, AI scores and pipeline status, and it is what the founder, admin and VC screens from Steps 4 to 8 all read and write. The migration creates or extends the table idempotently, adding the AI analysis columns. supabase-rls-policies.sql turns on row-level security with policies for owners, VCs and admins, so founders see only their own rows, VCs see approved ones and admins see everything. Those policies are the real security boundary, and the client-side role checks only add to them.
tour.languageLesson: Postgres row-level security attaches a USING/WITH CHECK predicate (for example auth.uid() = user_id) to every query on a table. Because the browser talks to the database directly with an anon key, RLS is what stops one user from reading another user's rows.

tour.title: Config and Deployment
tour.description: The frontend is a static Vite SPA. .env.example lists the Supabase URL and key, the Google client ID and the Spring Boot backend URL. vite.config.ts sets up the '@' path alias and splits vendor code into separate chunks. vercel.json builds into dist and rewrites every non-asset path to index.html so that the client-side routes from Step 2 work. The keep-alive.yml GitHub Actions workflow pings the Render backend every 10 minutes, which together with serverWarmup from Step 5 protects founders from cold-start errors.
tour.languageLesson: In GitHub Actions, 'on: schedule: - cron: "*/10 * * * *"' runs a workflow on a timer, and workflow_dispatch adds a manual Run button. Scheduled runs are best-effort and can be delayed, which is why the app also warms the server itself.
